title: Phantom Wolf
text: “This really is like something out of a story,” Rabbit Guy whispered to Crocodile Guy.
“That’s what legends are like. I’m in a similar boat myself.”
“Well, that’s true. Since it’s Wolf’s turn, I won’t say anything to tease him about it. I wonder how Iwatani-sama will respond.”
I looked over toward Panda and the others, only to find them looking off elsewhere. What were they doing, I wondered, when—
“It’s probably best to stop wallowing in sentiment about now,” said Older Sister.
“Something’s approaching, I say!”
“Vof!?”
“Ah, so the monster in question has shown itself.”
And so, with no time left for sentimentality, the monster came at us. Its form was that of a great wolf made of black shadow.
“Vuvuvuvu…”

The monster’s name was… oh? I couldn’t quite make it out properly. Faintly, it seemed to read Phantom Wolf. But… what was this feeling? A flash crossed my mind—something like the monster I’d seen back during the loop when we went to Faubrey, at Big Sister’s secret base, the one that had used Big Sister as a vessel for Big Sister’s Friend’s soul. Was it just my imagination?
“Vou!”
“Best to finish it in one blow, I say!”
It had been a while since I’d used Brionac to blast something away. This thing seemed to carry some kind of ghost-type or dark attribute.
“Wait, hold on, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Take this, I say. Brionac!”
“No, wa—!?”
“Hey, given the situation, you should watch a little more—”
“Vofu!?”

Take my Brionac, I say! And so I unleashed Brionac at Phantom Wolf—I thought it landed with a solid hit, but in a burst the shadow dispersed and reappeared right beside it. What was this? It was the same strange sensation as when I’d tried attacking Big Sister in earnest and she’d dodged.
“It dodged!? Dodging Motoyasu-kun’s attack, that’s impressive.”
“I won’t lose, I say! Coming at you again in succession! Take my Chaos Stab, I say!”
I closed the distance in one smooth motion.
“No wait, Motoyasu-kun—”
Shu-shu-shu! I struck, but it dodged the same way. Still, I managed to graze it.
“Vo… VOOOOOH—!?”
“A solid hit, I say! Here I come!”
“I said don’t come!”
Father scolded me. And just as I looked away for a moment, Phantom Wolf seized the opening and struck me with its front paw, sending me flying. No damage, but it was quite the powerful blow.
“Hold on, Motoyasu-kun, stay.”
“Understood, I say.”
Standby, then.
“Hard to tell which one’s the mad dog here,” said Rabbit Guy.
“Indeed,” said Crocodile Guy.
“Vo… Vuvuvu…” Phantom Wolf let out a low growl. It was intimidating us. While I stood by, what exactly was Father trying to do, I wondered?
“So, Wolf. You’ve encountered the target in question—what will you do? I can hold it down if you need me to, you know?”
Father wanted to let Wolf handle this one himself. As for Wolf, he wore a fearful expression and was trembling. Honestly, how pathetic.
“Ugh…”

“I want to confirm what kind of monster this really is—I might be overthinking it and there’s a chance it’s something else entirely. Or… is it Wolf’s wish to have Motoyasu-kun finish it off without ever finding out?”
Wolf shot Father a resentful look at the question.
“To be honest… I’m the older brother between us siblings, technically. So I understand the feelings of an older brother, but as for the feelings of a younger brother—honestly, all I can do is guess.”
Here, for some reason, Father started talking about being an older brother among siblings.
“Huh?”
“Ah?”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy furrowed their brows at Father’s words.
“If anything, I’d say he knows already. He’s certainly reliable, but he also lets people rely on him.”
“Right?”
“Or is that exactly what he’s getting at?”
“Maybe… I’m fairly sure he understands, but—no, I’m not entirely free of doubts when it comes to the younger brother I’ve only heard about secondhand.”
“Given how suspicious it is that he hasn’t caught on, he might really only recognize him as an older brother figure—more like the kind of reliance you’d place on a relative or a parent.”

Father shot the two of them a brief glance as they whispered among themselves, a look that seemed to carry some complaint. As for me, if anything, I understood the feelings of an older brother myself—having spent my days with those mysterious pigs who’d appointed themselves my little sisters.
“Vo, Vofu.”
Wolf clenched his fists tightly and took a step forward.
“…That would be meaningless. I’m scared… All these different feelings mixed together—I never thought confirming the truth could be this frightening.”
But… I don’t want to look away. Wolf continued on like that. Then Wolf turned to face Phantom Wolf and readied himself.
“Awooooooooooooo!”
“Awoooooooooooooooo!”

As if in answer, Phantom Wolf let out a howl, and Wolf howled back—then the two of them charged and clashed head-on. With a keening sound, the claws on Wolf’s hand turned translucent, and matching translucent claws appeared on Phantom Wolf’s paw.
“So this is the trial the Claw has bestowed… I’ll do my best! Voff!”
Wolf readied himself with eyes full of resolve.
“Haaaaaaaaaa!”
“Gaaaaaaaaa!”

Bam! A body slam, followed by clashing claws, biting, kicking—Wolf and Phantom Wolf traded blows one after another. Hmm… were they holding back, I wondered? It seemed like Wolf ought to be able to win easily, and yet the exchange dragged on. Eventually, Phantom Wolf’s darkness swelled in a burst, and it shifted into a werewolf form. What kind of monster was this, I wondered?
“Ha! Awoooooon!”
“Awooooooooon!”
As Wolf and the werewolf-form Phantom Wolf each howled, something like a faint moon rose dimly into the sky and rained down upon them both.
“Is that some kind of buff magic?”
“I believe so—Wolf did mention there was a unique magic passed down through his family, if I recall.”

“Something called Howling Moon—whether it counts as magic or a skill, it’s apparently that sort of thing. It boosts abilities and induces an excited state, and for anyone around with an aptitude for beastification, it also offers assistance with transformation.”
“That’s the famous one from Wolf’s family,” Elephant remarked.
So there was such a magic. I see.
“In that case, the opponent really is what we suspected—it’s matching the Claw too.”
Father seemed to have some idea of what was going on. But there was something I found extremely concerning.
“If it can turn translucent and split like that, hand it over to Filo-tan, I say!”
“Motoyasu-kun, you really can’t read the room, can you…”
Father said to me in a tone like Panda’s. What was wrong with that? It was for Filo-tan’s weapon, after all.
“Though the performance would probably be worse,” said Crocodile Guy.
“Probably,” said Rabbit Guy.
“What a farce…” said Older Sister. “Well, I suppose they have to fight it out until they’re satisfied. Better than some bloody fated duel to the death, isn’t it?”
“It’s probably the kind of trial Rafumi-san mentioned, meant to draw out its full potential. Let’s just watch quietly.”
“Okay!” Kou nodded at Elephant’s words.
“Vau!”
“Vauuuuuu!”
And so Wolf and Phantom Wolf collided head-on once more, trading claws and kicks in another exchange.
“Kyan!” But Wolf seemed to be losing ground and got sent flying.
